title: Professional Email and Harborline Domains: DNS Records and Mail Routing
content:
Mail operations note on how a Professional Email subscription meets the domain it uses.

**DNS records.** Where the product sets up records automatically for a Harborline domain on Harborline DNS, and the subscription's linked Harborline domain is active and on Harborline DNS nameservers, the MX, SPF, DKIM and autodiscover records are set at activation; otherwise the customer sets them at their DNS provider.

**Hosting mailboxes.** Once the subscription takes over the domain's MX, any cPanel mailboxes of a Harborline hosting plan for the same domain stop receiving mail, so the two never run side by side for one domain.

**Domain state.** A domain that is expired, in redemption or transferred out stops delivering mail for every subscription that uses it, without changing the subscription's billing.

## Decision table for the DNS records

| Linked Harborline domain | Domain status | Nameservers | Records |
|---|---|---|---|
| present | active | Harborline DNS | set by Harborline at activation |
| present | active | external | set by the customer at their DNS provider |
| present | not active | any | set by the customer at their DNS provider |
| none (domain registered elsewhere) | not applicable | not applicable | set by the customer at their DNS provider |

## Example (hypothetical)

A Harborline Mail Plus subscription for a domain registered elsewhere is activated: the customer adds the MX, SPF, DKIM and autodiscover records at their own DNS provider. If that domain later lapses, mail stops arriving while the subscription's billing continues unchanged.
